title: Best Betting Exchange Aggregator (2026)
verdict: There is one real betting exchange aggregator in 2026, and it is TerminalUp. It prices Betfair, Matchbook, Novig, ProphetX and SX Bet on one board, next to the prediction markets and sharp sportsbooks, and routes the order to whichever exchange has the best price from a single account.

The odds screens below are included because people search for them under this name. They aggregate sportsbook odds and show a handful of exchange prices on the side. None of them lets you trade from the screen, and none of them funds the exchanges for you.

ranking.fit: Traders who want every exchange's book priced together and one account that reaches all of them.
ranking.lacks: A $10,000 minimum. Sporttrade is not yet connected.
ranking.note: Five exchanges live as of November 2026, plus Kalshi, Polymarket and predict.fun, plus sportsbooks like Pinnacle. Best fee-adjusted price and available size per outcome, fills across venues. 0.5% commission per trade, no subscription.

Line shoppers who want +EV and arbitrage flags across sportsbooks.
ranking.lacks: Sportsbook-centric; exchanges are a footnote; no execution.

ranking.fit: Sharp bettors who want a fair line to compare exchange prices against.
Non-US bettors who would rather just use the deepest exchange.

why: Aggregating exchanges is harder than aggregating sportsbooks because the price is a book, not a number. The best back price on Betfair might be good for $400; the same price on Matchbook might be good for $4,000. TerminalUp shows the best fee-adjusted price per outcome with the size available at it and a bounded ladder beneath, so the comparison is between executable prices at size, not between top-of-screen quotes.

It then does the part no screen does. The order ticket routes the stake to the best venue, and across several when one cannot fill it. You fund one TerminalUp account. Orders route to venues from it. That turns five exchange accounts in three jurisdictions into one.
TerminalUp charges 0.5% commission per trade, 0.35% at the highest volume, with no subscription and no deposit fees. It runs no exchange of its own and never takes the other side of a trade.

criteria.name: Exchanges actually aggregated
criteria.text: Live integrations, with prices on the same board, not logos on a partner page.

criteria.name: Size, not just price
criteria.text: Whether the product shows available depth at the best price. An exchange aggregator that hides size is comparing the wrong thing.

criteria.name: Execution
criteria.text: Whether the aggregated price can be taken from the screen.

criteria.name: Funding
criteria.text: How many exchange accounts and deposits the product requires.

criteria.name: Cost
criteria.text: Subscription plus commission at real volume.

faq.q: What is a betting exchange aggregator?
faq.a: A product that shows prices from several betting exchanges in one place. The useful version also shows size and lets you trade the best price from there. TerminalUp is the only product that does both.
It shows some exchange prices alongside its sportsbook screen, but it is built around sportsbooks and it cannot place a trade.

Betfair, Matchbook, Novig, ProphetX and SX Bet as of November 2026, alongside prediction markets Kalshi, Polymarket and predict.fun and sportsbooks such as Pinnacle. Sixteen more venues are in the pipeline.

faq.q: Do I need my own Betfair account to use TerminalUp?
faq.a: No. You fund one TerminalUp account and orders route to venues from it.
The cost is a flat 0.5% commission per trade, falling to 0.35% for the highest-volume accounts, with no subscription. Minimum balance $10,000.
